title: continuous-batcher-scheduler-tuning-queueing-fairness-starvation-timeouts
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production traffic analysis surfaced two recurring issues with the continuous batcher scheduler: (1) long-tail latency spikes caused by head-of-line blocking when a small number of large requests dominated batch composition, and (2) starvation of low-priority/short requests during high throughput bursts. This PR implements scheduler-side queueing and fairness improvements plus conservative timeout controls to reduce p99 latency and prevent starvation. Summary of changes: added a short-duration acceptance window (queueing window) to the continuous batcher so that small requests can join an in-progress batch within a configurable delta_ms instead of waiting for the next batch cycle; implemented per-request priority metadata and token-aware fairness that limits how much capacity a single priority class can occupy in a rolling window; introduced starvation detection and requeueing logic with an exponential backoff cap (configurable starvation_ttl_ms, max_requeues) to ensure long-waiting requests eventually trigger a forced dispatch or fallback; added per-request max_wait_ms and a soft_timeout path to allow graceful partial responses or fallback to smaller model variants; centralized admission controller for the batcher to decide hot-path vs slow-path and to fall back to non-batched execution when batching would increase tail latency. KV-cache and kernel compatibility: added a scheduling hint that preserves KV-cache locality for requeued requests (when possible) to avoid cache rewarm penalties; ensured kernel selection path respects requeue and slow-path semantics to avoid choosing quantized kernels that increase latency variance. Observability and metrics: new metrics (batcher.queue_window_ms.p50/p95/p99, batcher.fairness_share_ratio, batcher.starvation_requeues_total, batcher.requeue_success_rate, batcher.soft_timeouts) plus detailed tracing spans to correlate request priority, queue time, and kernel choice. Testing and benchmarks: unit and integration tests added for admission controller, starvation logic, and timeouts; perf harness runs on benchmark-lab show ~12% reduction in p99 end-to-end latency for mixed short/long workloads and no regression on median latency. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind continuous_batcher_v2 flag, staged canary to 10% of production traffic on dedicated pools for 48h with fallback to v1 on error, then ramp to 100% if SLAs are met. Backwards compatibility: scheduler tuning is opt-in via config; defaults are conservative to preserve existing behavior. See release notes below.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Overall this looks promising. Two asks: can you add an integration test that simulates continuous arrival of large requests while low-priority short requests try to enter? I want to see the measured fairness ratios.
Maya Chen: Added perf harness scenario in test/perf/mixed_workload_bench.cc and a unit test that asserts fairness caps are enforced. See commits c8a92b0 and f6e3d45.
Priya Nair: We need to ensure KV-cache locality hint doesn't accidentally leak model internals across tenants. Please validate isolation and add comments.
Maya Chen: Confirmed isolation preserved; locality hint is opaque and only used to prefer same-host placement when requeueing. Added comment and test in locality_hint.h.
Liam O'Connor: CI flake on linting for long function name; otherwise approve after small tweak to metric name. (Approved)

benchmarks: Mixed workload (10k requests): p50 unchanged, p95 -6%, p99 -12% compared to continuous_batcher_v1 (canary environment)
Throughput: no measurable regression under steady-state; batching efficiency improved for mixed sizes by ~8%
KV-cache warmup: requeue locality hint reduced cache-miss penalty by 30% in requeue scenarios
release_notes: Improved continuous batcher scheduling with queueing window and priority-aware fairness to reduce p99 latency in mixed workloads.
New config knobs: queue_window_ms, max_priority_share, starvation_ttl_ms, max_requeues, max_wait_ms, enable_soft_timeouts.
Backwards compatible and feature-flagged (continuous_batcher_v2). Can be safely canaried and rolled back.
Observability: new metrics for queueing and starvation; update dashboards to include batcher.queue_window_ms and batcher.starvation_requeues_total.
notes_for_ops: Enable behind continuous_batcher_v2 flag. Canary on dedicated GPU pools for 48h. Watch metrics: batcher.starvation_requeues_total, batcher.fairness_share_ratio, request_soft_timeouts. If p99 increases or requeue rate > 0.1% for sustained period, rollback flag.
